sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Personal Electronics and Smart Gadgets

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 180-190-1 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies; EU AML framework as transposed.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized deed of incorporation and articles of association (acte constitutif and statuts), filed electronically with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SARL minimum subscribed capital is EUR 12,000; at least 25% of the capital must be paid in on incorporation and held in a blocked Luxembourg bank account until the RCS certificate is issued; cash contributions may remain callable thereafter subject to the Company Law capital maintenance rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED unanimously in the first constituent meeting of LU_SARL: (1) The capital subscriptions and the draft articles of association are approved. (2) The minimum subscribed capital of EUR 12,000, with not less than 25% paid in, shall be lodged in a blocked account and released only after RCS registration. (3) The registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg. (4) [Name] is appointed Manager (gérant), with sole authority to bind the company, including opening bank accounts, filing regulatory submissions and applying for the business establishment permit. (5) All acts taken prior to incorporation are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and notarial draft preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary and LBR/RCS name index via the Luxembourg Business Registers portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators select the legal form SARL and a corporate name. The notary performs an online RCS name availability check, screens against protected names, and prepares the draft articles of association in French or German. AML/KYC files are opened for each shareholder and proposed manager.
required_dossiers: Valid passport copy of each incorporator
Draft business plan and object clause for online consumer electronics retail
Beneficial owner identification and ownership structure
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as identical or misleading, the notary submits a reserved alternative name and amends the draft articles within three business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked capital escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution selected by the shareholders (e.g. Banque Internationale à Luxembourg or other licensed bank).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The bank opens a temporarily blocked account in the name of the company to be formed or in the name of the subscribers, receives at least EUR 3,000 of paid-in capital, and issues a blocked-funds certificate to the notary. For larger share premiums, the full premium must be deposited before notarization.
required_dossiers: Bank KYC forms and confirmation of no tax offenses
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional source-of-funds evidence, the subscribers provide bank statements and tax documents; the escrow balance is corrected and an updated certificate is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary appointed by the incorporating shareholders.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All shareholders and the proposed manager appear before the notary or through a duly notarized power of attorney. The notary verifies legal capacity, the AML file, absence of professional prohibition, and receipt of the blocked-funds certificate. The final articles are read, approved, and signed as an authentic notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Criminal record extracts of the proposed manager
Declaration of non-disqualification from managing a Luxembourg company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any shareholder or manager fails validation, the signatory is replaced or the deed is postponed; the notary prepares a rectification or supplementation deed without additional statutory publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration, legal publication and release of capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), RCS section, through the notary's electronic filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the authenticated deed, registration form, and supporting legal declarations to the RCS. The RCS controls the legality of the incorporation and the statutory particulars, then registers LU_SARL, allocates an RCS number, and publishes the statutory notice in the RESA. The bank releases the blocked funds upon presentation of the RCS certificate.
required_dossiers: RCS electronic registration form (new company creation)
Lease or ownership document for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query on the object clause or legal form, the notary files corrections and a supplementary resolution with the RCS within ten days; a re-filing fee may apply only if a new publication is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation business permits and tax registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy, Direction générale des PME; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA; Centre commun de la sécurité sociale; MyGuichet.lu one-stop portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon obtaining the RCS extract, the company applies for the business establishment permit, registers for VAT, and submits the beneficial owner declaration to the Register of Beneficial Owners. The manager then executes the corporate governance file, including the shares register, first RCS filings, and official appointment documentation. If employees are hired, the company registers with the social security center.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of articles of association
Criminal record extract of the manager
Identity documents of the manager and shareholders
Proof of operational premises or registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the establishment permit is queried because the object clause is too broad or the manager lacks professional standing, the company submits a narrowed object or designated manager evidence, and exercises the administrative right to be heard within 15 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Direction générale des PME (General Directorate for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises), authority issuing the business establishment permit.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Establishment Permit (Autorisation d'établissement) for commercial e-commerce retail of consumer electronics; no separate sectoral electronics retail license applies.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Administration), under the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA; the proposed online retail operation falls below Grand-Ducal Regulation thresholds for retail and warehousing, but must register as a waste producer if packaging or WEEE quantities exceed household thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero process wastewater or manufacturing emissions; sanitary effluents discharged only to municipal sewer with consent; compliance with EU WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU for take-back and recycling; packaging waste recovery rates per Luxembourg packaging regulation; no VOC-emitting refurbishing processes on site.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) for storage areas and retail dispatch premises; occupational health inspection by Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM); structural load inspection for shelving and mezzanines; public liability and employer liability insurance coverage confirmed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct income taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and indirect taxes; unified digital taxpayer portal: MyGuichet and guichet.lu; corporate registry: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS) via eJustice.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the SARL: (1) execute the notarial deed of incorporation with minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 fully subscribed and paid up; (2) file for registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) through the eJustice/LBR electronic platform, which automatically issues the national business matricule (numéro d'identification) and transmits data to the ACD and AEDT; (3) the matricule functions as the tax identification number (TIN) for income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax purposes; (4) for VAT, submit the VAT registration application (Form 100) to the AEDT Service de la TVA via MyGuichet, which issues a separate Luxembourg VAT identification number with the 'LU' prefix plus eight digits; (5) foreign/non-resident entities making taxable supplies in Luxembourg without a local establishment must register directly for VAT online; non-EU suppliers must appoint an approved Luxembourg fiscal representative for VAT unless covered by the EU OSS/IOSS or electronic services simplification; (6) activate the MyGuichet business account for electronic filing of VAT returns, EC Sales Lists, and audited financial statements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the SARL is a resident capital company (société de capitaux) fully subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) at 17% plus a 7% solidarity surcharge, municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) at rates varying by commune (typically 6.75%-11.2%, approx. 6.75% in Luxembourg City), and annual net wealth tax (0.5% on excess net wealth above EUR 500,000). Pass-through treatment is not available. Territorial_Scope: resident SARL is taxed on worldwide income, mitigated by the participation exemption (exemption of qualifying dividends under Article 166 LIR and of qualifying capital gains under Article 166bis LIR subject to a 10% shareholding or EUR 6 million acquisition price and 12-month holding period) and by the European Parent-Subsidiary Directive eliminating withholding tax on outbound profit distributions. Tax_Exempt_Zone: no general tax-free zone applies in Luxembourg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Luxembourg law. Available elective regimes: (1) fiscal unity / group taxation election under Article 164bis LIR for EU-resident groups with a 95% direct or indirect holding between a Luxembourg parent and Luxembourg-resident subsidiaries or Luxembourg permanent establishments of EU companies, enabling income and losses to be pooled; (2) election to apply the single taxable person (assujetti unique) VAT grouping regime under Article 60 of the VAT law for affiliated entities; (3) application of the participation exemption is made through the corporate income tax return (Form 400/410) with supporting evidence, not by separate filing; (4) option to apply the deemed interest deduction (notional interest deduction) on new equity capital in the tax return; (5) hybrid mismatch neutralization elections and adjustments are mandated under the ATAD Grand-Ducal regulations of 2019, with no elective opt-out for in-scope mismatches; (6) by-erogation transactions relief: an entity may apply for an advance tax ruling from the ACD (tax rulings commission) to confirm the tax classification of cross-border flows before implementing the structure.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée - TVA) governed by the amended law of 12 February 1979 transposing the EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold for taxable persons established in Luxembourg: VAT registration is compulsory from the first taxable supply (effective from inception for a Luxembourg-resident SARL). For intra-EU distance sales of goods (B2C e-commerce) to consumers in other Member States, the pan-EU threshold is EUR 10,000 per calendar year; below this threshold, the supply remains subject to Luxembourg VAT; above it, the destination Member State's VAT applies via the One-Stop-Shop (OSS). For imports of low-value consignments (intrinsic value up to EUR 150), the Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) regime is available. Non-resident suppliers have no de minimis threshold for registration where they make any taxable supply in Luxembourg without OSS coverage.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), API stamping, or digital stamping regime is currently in force in Luxembourg. E-invoicing (facturation électronique) is legally accepted where the authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and legibility are preserved through reliable audit trails. B2G e-invoicing is mandatory for suppliers to national public authorities via the PEPPOL network (national eFactura platform). Luxembourg has not yet passed domestic legislation mandating structured e-invoicing for all B2B transactions; however, under the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) proposal, mandatory e-invoicing for intra-EU B2B/B2C transactions and related reporting is expected from 2028 (subject to final adoption), and the AEDT is preparing its ICT infrastructure accordingly.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0%) is available for: (1) direct exports of goods by the SARL to customers outside the EU, where the goods are dispatched or transported out of the EU by the supplier, the customer, or a third party acting on their behalf, with proof of physical exit from EU territory retained before the end of the reporting period deadline; (2) intra-EU B2B dispatches of goods where the SARL obtains the customer's valid EU VAT identification number, issues an accurate invoice, and reports the supply in the EC Sales List and Intrastat where thresholds apply; (3) certain services directly related to exported goods or supplied to non-EU business customers under the general place-of-supply rules (B2B services to non-EU recipients are outside Luxembourg VAT), which cover merchant fees and ancillary logistics services. B2C online retail exports to non-EU consumers qualify for 0% only where the shipment is accompanied by verifiable destination-country delivery evidence; shipments merely declared as export without independent transport confirmation are denied. Intra-EU B2C distance sales are not zero-rated but are taxable at destination and reported through OSS. The substantiation record must be kept for at least 10 years.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/electronic export declaration filed through Luxembourg Customs / ICS2) with the MRN (Movement Reference Number) for each shipment outside the EU
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR consignment note, or postal/courier export receipt showing the actual dispatch route
Commercial invoice and export sales contract with clear identification of buyer and consignee
Proof of arrival at destination (delivery confirmation, signed POD, customs entry in the destination country, or courier tracking report)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment/foreign exchange receipt evidencing settlement of the export proceeds in the SARL's Luxembourg bank account
Export Accompanying Document (EAD) and, where applicable, Intrastat declarations and EC Sales List references for intra-EU movements
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and Luxembourg Customs jointly scrutinize export zero-rating claims with particular attention to consumer-electronics e-commerce flows. Any failure to produce the mandatory customs documentation bundle, or any inconsistency in dates, volumes, or consignee identity, triggers retroactive reassessment at the standard 17% VAT rate, denial of the corresponding input VAT deduction, and collection of default interest on the under-declared VAT (statutory monthly late-payment interest accruing from the original due date until payment). Administrative fines range up to EUR 100,000 depending on the intent classification and the amount of tax evaded. Deliberate fraudulent schemes (forged customs declarations, insertion of fictitious export consignees, artificial reversal of circular transactions, or sham warehouse operations outside the EU) constitute criminal tax fraud under Luxembourg tax criminal law, punishable with imprisonment of up to 5 years and monetary penalties of up to EUR 250,000 per offence, plus the publication of the sanction, disqualification of managers, and clawback of all VAT exemptions and refunds previously granted for the audited period. The same documentation deficit can trigger cross-border customs duty recovery and notification to other Member States under VAT administrative cooperation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), the Eurosystem national central bank for the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; prudential supervision of banks, payment institutions and e-money institutions is delegated to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), while the European Central Bank (ECB) exercises ultimate monetary and foreign-reserve policy authority for the euro area.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg operates no exchange-control statute. Both current-account and capital-account convertibility are unrestricted under Articles 63 to 66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU); the euro is fully convertible. Interest, royalties, dividends and liquidation proceeds may be paid to any non-resident without BCL authorisation. The only practical hurdles to outward profit remittance are (i) documentary AML/CFT compliance under the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02, and (ii) Luxembourg dividend withholding tax at a 15% standard rate, reduced to 0% for qualifying EU corporate shareholders under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or to lower treaty rates for treaty-protected investors.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export-proceeds surrender obligation, mandatory repatriation timeline or obligatory conversion ratio applies in Luxembourg. The LU SARL may retain USD proceeds derived from Stripe and PayPal settlements indefinitely and convert them at its commercial discretion. Statutory friction is limited to balance-of-payments statistical reporting: Luxembourg-based payment service providers must report to the BCL, under Regulation (EC) No 184/2005 as implemented by BCL circular instructions, each cross-border payment above EUR 12,500 with an economic-purpose classification; no conversion of export receipts is mandated by law.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational EUR/USD Treasury Account with SEPA and SWIFT clearing
Operational Treasury Account with Trade-Finance Desk supporting documentary letters of credit; Capital Escrow Account available
Operational Account with multi-currency capabilities and merchant-settlement connectivity; Capital Escrow Account available
Operational Account with FX hedging execution and cash-pooling; Capital Escrow Account available
Digital-first Operational Account optimised for high-volume aggregator settlements; Capital Escrow Account available
Operational Account for domestic SME banking; limited trade-finance and FX desk

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High. Luxembourg recognises e-money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions authorised by the CSSF under PSD2 (Law of 1 August 2018 on payment services and e-money, Directive (EU) 2015/2366), and EMIs established elsewhere in the EEA may passport their services into Luxembourg. Legal constraints: an EMI may not take deposits or grant commercial loans; client funds must be safeguarded in segregated accounts at an EU credit institution or be covered by equivalent insurance; and direct TARGET2 access is generally unavailable, requiring an intermediary banking partner. For the SARL's treasury, a CSSF-licensed or passported EMI can optimise currency conversion and accelerate the Settlement of Stripe and PayPal payouts, but core clearing, documentary-credit issuance and capital-escrow functionality require a full commercial-banking relationship at BCEE, BIL, BNP Paribas Luxembourg, Société Générale Bank & Trust, ING or Raiffeisen. The recommended structure therefore uses an EMI as a secondary liquidity accelerator, not as the primary clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: CSSF Regulation 12-02 and the CSSF's remote-onboarding guidance permit electronic identification via eIDAS-qualified signatures and video-KYC, yet the standard onboarding practice of Luxembourg credit institutions requires an in-person compliance interview for at least one director and the designated AML point of contact; all UBOs holding 25% or more of the share capital must be identified, and in most banks will also be interviewed physically at the Luxembourg branch. A fully remote opening is possible only on a case-by-case basis with prior compliance-committee approval, typically where the group already holds a Luxembourg banking relationship. Budget two to four weeks for completion of the bank's standard corporate KYC across all signatories and UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque shareholder chain or non-EU beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised chain-of-title organisational chart; Luxembourg RCS extracts (extrait du registre de commerce et des sociétés); updated register of shareholders; passport and proof-of-residence for every UBO holding 25% or more; source-of-wealth memorandum for each UBO; independent legal opinion if any corporate intermediate is incorporated in a high-risk jurisdiction; the complete trace of all funding wires.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverifiable source of the SARL's initial capital subscription
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised deed of incorporation and subscription; bank confirmation of the exact capital deposit; certified bank statements of the contributing shareholders; board resolution approving the capital call; where contributed by a parent entity, the parent's audited financial statements and a formal intra-group contribution or loan agreement; RCS-filed UBO declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency micro-payment flows and chargeback volatility from Stripe/PayPal aggregation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed merchant agreements with Stripe and PayPal; 12-month projected settlement and chargeback model; documented transaction-monitoring policy aligned with CSSF Regulation 12-02; e-commerce refund and dispute-resolution procedure; daily reconciliation of aggregator settlement files against the SARL's accounting ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP or negative-news screening hits on counterparties, UBOs or beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Official sanctions-screening output from EU consolidated lists, UN lists and OFAC SDN where applicable; negative-news search report; sworn non-PEP declarations; for identified PEPs, submission to the bank's senior-management approval with an enhanced-monitoring plan under Article 5 of the Law of 12 November 2004.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-diversion and grey-market risk inherent to consumer-electronics retail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier onboarding file with invoices, Incoterms and HS codes (8471 automatic data-processing machines, 8517 telephone sets); distributor and end-customer country-screening; customs-broker compliance letters for export shipments; audit-ready record of each high-value shipment to justify the low-risk e-commerce classification.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity contributions are routed by SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank to the SARL's capital-escrow or operational IBAN at the Luxembourg credit institution, with an ISO 20022 purpose code CAPA (capital payment) or EQUI (equity-related flow) and remittance text restricted to the corporate name, RCS number and reference to the notarised deed. The receiving bank verifies the originator against the filed UBO and shareholder register and records the flow in the BCL balance-of-payments statistical return; funds are released to the operational account after the notarial deed and applicable confirmations are sighted. For intra-group shareholder loans, the route instead uses purpose code LEND and must be supported by a written intercompany loan agreement to avoid recharacterisation by the Luxembourg tax administration; third-party contributions in cryptocurrency or from non-bank channels are not accepted by clearing banks.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EU supplier payments are cleared via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) to the supplier's IBAN; extra-EU supplier invoices are settled by SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers; high-value supplier contracts and cross-border import transactions above the bank's threshold are supported by commercial documentary letters of credit under UCP 600, issued by BCEE, BIL or BNP Paribas Luxembourg with the SARL's operational account as applicant. Daily proceeds from Stripe and PayPal are swept by the aggregators' acquiring banks via SEPA or SWIFT to the SARL's operational account with descriptive settlement files; the SARL then applies its liquidity policy by maintaining a chargeback buffer in EUR and converting surplus USD through the relationship bank's FX desk. Intra-EEA urgent cash needs can be executed by SEPA Instant Credit Transfer; non-euro disbursements in restricted currencies are routed via an intermediate clearing bank through MT103 and, where required, a correspondent bank's nostro account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD forward with physical delivery, covering the USD settlement stream from Stripe and PayPal, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or an FX Master Agreement with the relationship bank

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) for receivables in restricted offshore-convertible currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, NGN) where local physical settlement is prohibited; cash-settled in EUR against a reference index
Cross-currency interest-rate swap (EUR/USD CCIRS) to hedge longer-term USD-denominated vendor financing or significant USD receivable programs
Plain-vanilla EUR/USD call and put options for asymmetric hedging of residual currency exposure, subject to MiFID II suitability and documented treasury-policy approval
Short-term FX swap (swap of spot versus forward EUR/USD) for managing rolling USD liquidity without leaving an open foreign-exchange position

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes, and management report where required) filed through eCDF and published in the electronic compendium
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end; for a calendar-year SARL no later than 30 June of the following year (if shareholder approval occurs earlier, within one month of approval)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: RCS late-filing notice, administrative fines up to EUR 5,000, referral to the public prosecutor, civil liability of managers, and eventual compulsory strike-off or judicial dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return covering Luxembourg corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC), net wealth tax (IFF), and minimum net wealth tax settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year SARLs, due no later than 31 May following the tax year with extensions available at the ACD's discretion for e-filing and tax advisers; different year-ends are due within the ACD published filing window after the close of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default tax assessment, late-payment interest at 10% per annum, administrative fines, enforced recovery, and personal/director liability for wilful non-compliance

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% national corporate income tax, plus municipal business tax (average 6.75%) and solidarity surcharge (7% of national CIT), yielding an aggregate effective rate of approximately 24.94% (2024).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard Luxembourg SARL has no general statutory tax holiday. Preferential regimes are limited to EU directives (parent-subsidiary participation exemption), IP box (80% exemption on qualifying IP income, effective ~5.2% without municipal tax), and notional interest deduction (NID) capped at 5% of new equity. Tax losses are actually available for carryforward without a fixed 5-year term; this schema placeholder is set to 5 for uniformity, but Luxembourg law permits indefinite carryforward (with annual utilization capped at 40% of taxable profit above EUR 1,000,000).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate income tax return – Form 402 (Impôt sur le revenu des collectivités); municipal business tax return – Form 500; net wealth tax return – Form 400. Mandatory e-filing via the MyGuichet.lu portal (or approved CAF-SAP interface).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed by the fifth month following the end of the fiscal year (e.g., 31 May for calendar-year taxpayers). Extensions may be granted upon proof of underlying financial statements; no automatic extension beyond 6-12 months without application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, RCS number, tax ID, legal form (SARL), direct shareholder details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must be identified by full name, country of residence, and TIN; treaty relief applications must be appended.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial profit per non-financial statements, adjusted for re-intégrations and deductibility limits (notably 50% non-deductible entertainment expenses, disallowed interest under ATAD cap).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned SARL, the full commercial profit is reported; treaty permanent establishment or participated ownership (participation exemption) is reflected via separate annexes, not this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of qualifying dividends and capital gains excluded under the Luxembourg participation exemption (EUR 10% or 12-month holding requirement).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claimable only if the SARL demonstrates substantive economic activity; non-resident incorporated holding companies must supply substance documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Notional interest deduction, R&D super-deduction, innovation certificates, foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Applies to the Luxembourg entity regardless of shareholder residence, subject to anti-abuse substance checks.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net wealth tax return (Form 400) on unitary net assets exceeding EUR 150,000, assessed at 0.5% (0.05% on excess over EUR 20 million for financial entities).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL is liable to net wealth tax even if entirely non-resident-owned.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing declaration and local file attestation, disclosing intercompany transactions, applied transfer pricing methods, subsidiaries/PECs and guarantees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Required if total related-party transactions exceed EUR 150,000 (aggregate) or group consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 750 million; same thresholds for non-resident controlled SARLs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties range from EUR 50 to EUR 5,000 per return; deliberate failure/submission of inaccurate returns: EUR 5,000 to EUR 250,000 plus criminal sanctions. Interest is levied at 0.6% per month on all overdue taxes, plus a 10% late-payment penalty. Habitual defaulters may face judicial injunction and director-level administrative fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic Luxembourg dividend withholding tax on distributions to shareholders, unless reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (condition: 10% shareholding, 12-month holding period, no abusive or artificial arrangement), or under Luxembourg participation exemption rules when the receiving EU parent is in comparable form.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the paying SARL must obtain from the beneficial owner a Luxembourg 'Certificate of Residence' (Form 770 by the receiving parent state) and submit the relevant treaty claim via the MyGuichet platform before payment. The Revenue must issue a reduced-withholding clearance (attestation de non-exonération or régime spécial); until clearance is granted, the 15% tax is withheld. Retroactive reimbursement is possible by filing Form 270 and supporting TRC plus affidavit of beneficial ownership and active substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 0% statutory dividend WHT? No – interest does not generate Luxembourg withholding tax at domestic level (none). Royalties (patents and trademarks): 15% statutory withholding tax for non-resident beneficiaries; under most Luxembourg DTAs treaty rates are reduced to 0%, 5% or 10% upon submission of the TRC. Loan interest to private shareholders is subject to additional abuse recharacterisation if thin-capitalised.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File arise when (i) consolidated group turnover exceeds EUR 750 million, and (ii) the Luxembourg entity has cross-border related-party transactions whose aggregate value exceeds EUR 150,000; a simplified three columns report is sufficient below such threshold. Benchmarks: EUR 150,000 (aggregate related-party transactions).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no standalone FDI/ESR regime, but the NPR (national legislation) imposes a general anti-abuse rule (Steueroasen-Abgabeverordnung, section 6 AbgO) and OECD Pillar Two GloBE requirements assume substance. The EU ATAD incorporates a substance test for treaty and participation claims; a SARL in digital retail must maintain actual senior management, employees, decision-making, office premises, and operational risk controlling outsourced logistics or warehousing. Local substance thresholds for TP documentation vary, but any inconsistency between substance and profit allocation is an immediate enforcement target.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate misdeclaration of intercompany sales (digital consumer electronics), fabrication of purchase invoices from round-trip trading files, under-declaration of Stripe/PayPal settlement revenue, or non-disclosure of foreign bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine from EUR 25,000 to EUR 1,000,000; administrative re-assessment with a 10% tax addition and 0.6% monthly interest; confiscation of goods and trading bans. Repeat offenders may have tax returns voided and assets attached.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de-facto managers face personal civil restitution for lost taxes; Luxembourg courts may order travel bans, asset freezes and imprisonment of up to 10 years for fraudulent bankruptcy-aggravated evasion, and manager ban from corporate boards for 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A Luxembourg SARL e-commerce retailer with low taxable margin, consistent losses or expense recharges to tax havens, while directing sales and inventory via a related-party Irish-Dutch joint venture; no local staff or real board decisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: TP adjustment to arm's length with a 20% surcharge (taxe additionnelle); interest at 0.6% monthly; denial of participation exemption and of EU Parent-Secondary Directive benefits; reclassification of service fees as deemed dividends or hidden distributions subject to 15% WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing an upwards adjustment waiver or knowingly executing a value-draining IP royalty scheme become jointly liable for the additional CIT, municipal business tax, net wealth tax and WHT; can be ordered to repay sums to the corporate estate in civil proceedings, and a criminal migration ban is possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Shell/Holding of Bank Account / Money Laundering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of the SARL as a funnelling vehicle in e-commerce involving buyers residing in high-risk jurisdictions, layered refund payments to shell entities, or allowing third-party chargebacks and invoice circularity without underlying contract or customs documents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Dissolution of the SARL (striking-off) with a penalty of EUR 10,000–100,000 under Luxembourg AML law (Loi du 12 novembre 2004, as amended); the beneficial owner is reported to the FIU (CRF); account frozen and seizure powers available; directors are subject to administrative fines of EUR 5,000–500,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign bank attestations of untruthful BO declarations expose themselves to personal criminal liability for money laundering (up to 5 years imprisonment) and personal civil liability for the sums laundered; they may be prohibited from travelling to the EU under Schengen-wide judicial co-operation frameworks.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to a non-resident parent (e.g., a shareholder in Switzerland or principal in a no-tax jurisdiction) without satisfying the 10% holding test, without sufficient substance of the parent, or before the 12-month QSD/QAPE holding period, while claiming 0% WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive WHT at 15% plus 50% penalty for abusive deduction; disallowance of the EU directive benefits; interest from actual payment date. Luxembourg tax authorities may request compulsory audit and seizure of bank guarantees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false beneficial-owner forms or misleading holding certificates are personally liable for the unpaid WHT, sanction surcharge and interest; Luxembourg case law has allowed criminal recovery against directors for restitution of the tax loss, with imprisonment of up to 5 years.
